General_Description.Text: SHANEL is a tissue clearing method driven by detergent permeabilization chemistry designed to clear and label stiff human organs. It enables centimeters-deep molecular labeling and clearing of whole human organs, rendering intact adult human brain and kidney transparent. The method allows for deep tissue penetration of labeling and clearing agents, making it suitable for performing 3D histology with antibodies and dyes in large, sturdy tissues.

Highlights: 'SHANEL renders intact adult human brain and kidney transparent'

Summary: 'To overcome these challenges, we developed SHANEL, a method based on a new tissue permeabilization approach to clear and label stiff human organs. We used SHANEL to render the intact adult human brain and kidney transparent and perform 3D histology with antibodies and dyes in centimeters-depth.'

Introduction: 'Here, we introduce SHANEL (small-micelle-mediated human organ efficient clearing and labeling), a new method that is driven by detergent permeabilization chemistry allowing the penetration of labeling and clearing agents into centimeters-thick mammalian organs. Our approach enables histology using dyes and antibodies in human samples ranging from 1.5 cm thickness to whole adult human organs.'

Tissue_Types.Text4: SHANEL works on  human samples ranging from 1.5 cm thickness to whole adult human organs and other large mammalian organs such as pig brain and pancreas.
Text4_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'Our approach enables histology using dyes and antibodies in human samples ranging from 1.5 cm thickness to whole adult human organs.We also show that the technology works on other large mammalian organs such as pig brain and pancreas, which can readily be labeled transgenically.'

Tissue_Types.Text5: post-mortem human brain and kidney specimens
Text5_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'It allows full penetration of labeling molecules and clearing chemicals into centimeters-sized decades-aged human tissues such as post-mortem human brain and kidney specimens.'

Text6_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'As pig is a much better model system for the human islets research compared to rodents, study of transgenic INS-EGFP pig pancreas in combination with SHANEL clearing can also accelerate research in metabolic disorders.'

Time_Consumption.Text1: SHANEL clearing provided rapid transparency of the 12.0 * 7.3 * 5.0 cm size pig brain within 1.5 months.
Text1_Reference: Development of SHANEL Tissue Clearing section: 'SHANEL clearing provided rapid transparency of the 12.0 * 7.3 * 5.0 cm size pig brain including heavily myelinated white matter, thalamus, and brainstem within 1.5 months.'

Time_Consumption.Text2: The whole process including labeling and clearing takes approximately 4 months for one adult human brain.
Text2_Reference: Generation of Intact Transparent Human Brain by SHANEL Clearing section: 'The whole process including labeling and clearing takes approximately 4 months and costs approximately 3,200 € for one adult human brain.'

Text3_Reference: METHOD DETAILS section, 'Pig brain clearing with passive SHANEL':'After the PBS washing performed at room temperature, the samples were shaken with a series of Ethanol (Merck, 10098535000)/DiH2O solutions (50%, 70%, 100%, 100% v/v) at room temperature, followed by a DCM (Roth, KK47.1) incubation and in the end they were immersed into the BABB (benzyl benzoate:benzyl alcohol = 2:1, Sigma, W213802, 24122) solution until complete transparency. The incubation time depended on the sample size: for whole brains, 4 days for each step were needed.'

Text4_Reference: METHOD DETAILS section, 'Active SHANEL clearing of pig pancreas':'The clearing was started with a series of 250 mL of Ethanol(EtOH)/DiH2O solutions (50%, 70%, 100%, 100% v/v) pumping for 6 hours at each step. Then the pancreas was passively incubated with DCM for 1 day, proceeded by incubation into BABB solution until complete transparency in around 2 weeks.'

Time_Consumption.Text5: 1.5 cm-thick intact human brain slice: 19 d
Text5_Reference: METHOD DETAILS section, 'Passive histology of a 1.5 cm-thick intact human brain slice':'The clearing started with dehydration using a series of 1 L of EtOH/DiH2O solutions (50%, 70%, 100%, 100% v/v) and followed by delipidation using 1 L DCM. Each step lasted 1 day. Then the samples were incubated in 1 L BABB solution at room temperature until completely transparency in around 2 weeks.'

Text6_Reference: METHOD DETAILS section, 'Passive SHANEL histology of intact human thyroid':'The clearing was started incubating the sample in a series solutions consisting of 200 mL of EtOH/DiH2O solutions (50%, 70%, 100%, 100% v/v), shaking for half day each step, followed by 200 mL of DCM for 5 hours, then proceeded with 200 mL BABB solution until complete transparency reached in 3-5 days.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text1: The dimensions of the pig brain after clearing became 7.5 * 5.0 * 3.3 cm, with a shrinkage ratio of approximately 30% in volume.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Development of SHANEL Tissue Clearing': 'The dimensions of the pig brain after clearing became 7.5 * 5.0 * 3.3 cm, with a shrinkage ratio of approximately 30% in volume.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text2: The final volume of the shrunken brain was 56% of the initial volume.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Generation of Intact Transparent Human Brain by SHANEL Clearing': 'The final volume of the shrunken brain was 56% of the initial volume.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text3: The ratiometric enlargement of shrunken tissues after SHANEL histology overlaid well with their pre-cleared images suggesting an isotropic tissue shrinkage.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'The ratiometric enlargement of shrunken tissues after SHANEL histology overlaid well with their pre-cleared images suggesting an isotropic tissue shrinkage.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text4: In addition, SHANEL-induced shrinkage (e.g., 44% reduction in volume for adult human brain) and usage of light-sheet microscopes with double-sided illumination could further facilitate imaging of the large, cleared human samples.
Text4_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'In addition, SHANEL-induced shrinkage (e.g., 44% reduction in volume for adult human brain) and usage of light-sheet microscopes with double-sided illumination could further facilitate imaging of the large, cleared human samples.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: Endogenous GFP signal was well preserved in CHAPS/NMDEA permeabilization solution but dramatically decreased after clearing, while the Atto647n fluorescence signal was preserved up to 11 months with nanoboosting after clearing.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Development of New Detergent Permeabilization Chemistry': 'Endogenous GFP signal was well preserved in CHAPS/NMDEA permeabilization solution but dramatically decreased after clearing...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: anti-GFP nanobodies conjugated with bright Atto dyes
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Development of New Detergent Permeabilization Chemistry': 'To enhance and stabilize the EGFP signal in centimeters-sized tissue, we used anti-GFP nanobodies conjugated with bright Atto dyes (Cai et al., 2019) (Figure S2C).'

Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Generation of Intact Transparent Human Brain by SHANEL Clearing': 'Then, we set up a pressure-driven pumping system to circulate all clearing reagents and cell nucleus labeling dye (TO-PRO-3) through the four arteries to accelerate the process (Figure 3A).'

Text4_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Methoxy-X04 (Jung et al., 2015; Klunk et al., 2002) and TO-PRO-3, which were affordable dyes in large quantities, to label Abeta plaques and cell nuclei, respectively, in an intact 16.5 3 16.5 3 1.5 cm human brain slice.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text5: Iba1 (ionized calcium binding adaptor molecule 1) antibody and PI (propidium iodide)
Text5_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Iba1 (ionized calcium binding adaptor molecule 1) antibody to immunolabel microglia (Figures 4C–4J) and PI (propidium iodide) to label cell nucleus.'

Text6_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Next, we used TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) antibody to immunolabel neuronal structures along with PI labeling of the cell nucleus (Figures 4K–4N).'

Text7_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Here, we used Lectin dye to effectively label a human brain sample with a size of 3.0*1.9*1.5 cm (Figure S5C).'

Text8_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Toward understanding the 3D cellular structures of the human kidney, we used SHANEL histology with active perfusion of TRITC-dextran and TO-PRO3 dyes through the renal artery to label the vessels and dense cellular structure of the glomeruli in the entire kidney with a size of 11.5 * 8.2 * 3.0 cm.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text9: primary rabbit antibody anti-Iba1 (1:1000, Wako, 019-19741), and the primary rabbit antibody anti-GFAP (1:1000, Dako, Z033401-2) respectively, followed by the secondary antibody Alexa 647 goat anti-rabbit (1:500, Life Technology, A31852)
Text9_Reference: METHOD DETAILS section, 'Passive SHANEL antibody histology of 1.5 cm-thick human brain samples':'For the evaluation of the deformation at the microscopic level, samples were labeled to highlight cellular structures: in particular microglia and astrocytes in the samples were stained using the primary rabbit antibody anti-Iba1 (1:1000, Wako, 019-19741), and the primary rabbit antibody anti-GFAP (1:1000, Dako, Z033401-2) respectively, followed by the secondary antibody Alexa 647 goat anti-rabbit (1:500, Life Technology, A31852) using the SHANEL histology protocol (see previous sections).'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text10: anti-Neuropeptide Y, anti-MBP (myelin basic protein), anti-laminin antibodies and PI

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text11: Hematoxylin & eosin (H&E), Nissl and Periodic Acid Schiff (PAS)

Preservation_Stability.Text1: We also found that the signal was stable for several months after SHANEL histology.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'These results demonstrate that SHANEL histology can successfully permeabilize the entire 1.5 cm thick sturdy human brain slices for deep tissue antibody labeling using diverse antibodies (Figure S5A). This represents a 1–2 order of magnitude enhancement in the thickness of adult human tissue that could be processed for histology compared with prior methods (Hildebrand et al., 2018). We also found that the signal was stable for several months after SHANEL histology (Figure S5B).'

Preservation_Stability.Text2: Finally, owing to the complete dehydration and incubation in organic solvents, the tissues are preserved by SHANEL histology, allowing long-term storage for the future studies by the same investigators or in other labs.
Text2_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'Finally, owing to the complete dehydration and incubation in organic solvents, the tissues are preserved by SHANEL histology, allowing long-term storage for the future studies by the same investigators or in other labs.'

Preservation_Stability.Text3: The Atto647n fluorescence signal was preserved up to 11 months with nanoboosting after clearing.
Text3_Reference: figure S2: 'Endogenous GFP signal was well preserved in CHAPS/NMDEA permeabilization solution but dramatically decreased after clearing, while the Atto647n fluorescence signal was preserved up to 11 months with nanoboosting after clearing (n = 3).'

Application.Text1: SHANEL enables centimeters deep molecular labeling and clearing of whole human organs, including the intact adult human brain and kidney, for 3D histology with antibodies and dyes.
Text1_Reference: Highlights section: 'SHANEL enables centimeters deep molecular labeling and clearing of whole human organs'
SUMMARY section: 'We used SHANEL to render the intact adult human brain and kidney transparent and perform 3D histology with antibodies and dyes in centimeters-depth.'

Application.Text2: SHANEL reveals structural details of the intact human eye, human thyroid, human kidney, and transgenic pig pancreas at cellular resolution.
Text2_Reference: SUMMARY section: 'Thereby, we revealed structural details of the intact human eye, human thyroid, human kidney, and transgenic pig pancreas at the cellular resolution.'

Application.Text3: SHANEL allows for the mapping of cellular and molecular architecture of large intact mammalian organs using deep learning and light-sheet microscopy.
Text3_Reference: Highlights section: 'Deep learning and light-sheet microscopy with SHANEL allows human organ mapping'
SUMMARY section: 'Furthermore, we developed a deep learning pipeline to analyze millions of cells in cleared human brain tissues within hours with standard lab computers.'

Application.Text4: SHANEL is used to study the 3D distribution of pancreatic beta cells within the islets of Langerhans in INS-EGFP transgenic pig pancreas, enabling quantification of islet volume and demonstration of islet size heterogeneity.
Text4_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Development of SHANEL Tissue Clearing': 'We demonstrated that the 3D distribution of pancreatic beta cells as single cell or groups of cells within the islets of Langerhans could be readily assessed by our new approach enabling quantification of islet volume and demonstration of islet size heterogeneity.'

Application.Text5: SHANEL facilitates the imaging of intact human organs, such as the whole adult human brain and kidney, using a prototype light-sheet microscope with extended sample holding capacity.
Text5_Reference: RESULTS section, '3D Reconstruction of Intact Human Organs and Analysis of Big Data Using Deep Learning': 'To enable the imaging of intact human organs, we used a prototype light-sheet microscope with extended stage movements and a large sample accommodation chamber.'

Application.Text6: Thus, our approach provides the basis for 3D histological assessment of the whole human brain in the near future.
Text6_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Generation of Intact Transparent Human Brain by SHANEL Clearing': 'Thus, our approach provides the basis for 3D histological assessment of the whole human brain in the near future.'

Application.Text7: Thus, SHANEL histology allows the labeling of specific molecules, cells, and vasculature in centimeters-sized human brain samples presenting a viable tool to scale up the investigation of brain pathologies.
Text7_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SHANEL Histology of Centimeters-Sized Human Organs': 'Thus, SHANEL histology allows the labeling of specific molecules, cells, and vasculature in centimeters-sized human brain samples presenting a viable tool to scale up the investigation of brain pathologies.'

Application.Text9: Thus, SHANEL technology can be a new tool to study pathologies of intact human organs at a gross scale proving valuable information to understand organ functions in health and disease.
Text9_Reference: RESULTS section, '3D Reconstruction of Intact Human Organs and Analysis of Big Data Using Deep Learning': 'Thus, SHANEL technology can be a new tool to study pathologies of intact human organs at a gross scale proving valuable information to understand organ functions in health and disease.'

Application.Text10: Thus, our approach can also tremendously help scaling up the efforts on Human Protein Atlas (HPA) by reducing the time to label and annotate across large human tissues.
Text10_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'Thus, our approach can also tremendously help scaling up the efforts on Human Protein Atlas (HPA) by reducing the time to label and annotate across large human tissues.'
